I enjoy adding garlic powder (Not garlic salt!)

Crack an egg onto the noodles right as soon as you take them off the heat.

Soft-boil an egg, slice it in half from top to bottom, place it in the ramen after cooking.

Drain the noodles after you cook them! It becomes a noodle dish instead of a soup. Mix the flavor packet into a little water, you may want to use it sparingly. Mix the noodles in with some flavoring (remember, less is more- you're no longer flavoring a bowl of water). Add veggies! Green onions. Water chestnuts. Baby corn.

You can throw Onions, Carrots, Celery, or other veggies in the pot mid-boil to really bring in some crunch and flavor.

Lemon Pepper can be a literal spice and a nice tang.

Cooking the ramen in chicken broth is a great substitute to the packets and leaves you the actual packet.

Lemons/Limes are nice too, cut them up and juice them into the bowl after cooking.

Worcestershire sauce is a nice peppery smoky flavor to mix with the noodles.

Bacon chunks (Other meats are generally too hard to crumble) adds great (diabetic) flavor.

Other than that, I invite you to experiment. Tell me what you think!

Does anyone know how to make a user flair "central" instead of individually making them for each single person? (if possible)

Yes, there are 2 things you can do:

  1. Combine the common styles into one rule,

  2. Target multiple elements per rule.

To combine the common styles we make use of the ^= attribute selector which matches the start of a string. Example:

#container a[href^="/user/"]::after {
 background: #67C8FF;
 border: 1px solid #67C8FF;
 border-radius: 2px;
 color: #FFFFFF;
 margin-left: 3px;
 margin-right: 3px;
 padding: 2px 4px;
 vertical-align: middle;
}

#container a[href="/user/ArkhamKnight"]::after {
 content: "Moderator";
}

#container a[href="/user/RedHood"]::after {
 content: "Joker";
}

The first rule means all links whose URLs begin with /user/ will have those styles applied. But due to the nature of the ::after pseudo-element, they will not be visible unless there is a content defined, so it will not affect other users without flair.

To give multiple people the same flair, simply join the selectors with a comma, like so:

#container a[href="/user/ArkhamKnight"]::after, #container a[href="/user/BruceWayne"]::after {
 content: "Moderator";
}
